subject: Chemistry
title: Three Mile Island: A Partial Meltdown
description: Learn Three Mile Island: A Partial Meltdown in one minute.

hook.text: In 1979, a stuck valve and misleading instruments caused a partial meltdown at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania.

buildup.text: A valve stuck open, draining coolant water. Operators saw a signal saying the valve was closed—it showed command, not status.

discovery.text: Without coolant, fuel rods overheated and partially melted. Half the reactor core was damaged before anyone realized.

twist.text: Little radiation escaped—containment held. But public fear surged. No new US reactors were ordered for 30 years.

climax.text: The accident proved that even 'safe' designs can fail from simple human-interface errors. Better displays saved future plants.

punchline.text: A stuck valve and a misleading light. Small design flaws caused a nuclear crisis.

quiz.question: What fundamental problem caused the Three Mile Island accident?
options: A valve stuck open and instruments showed the wrong status to operators
An earthquake damaged the reactor cooling system
Workers accidentally withdrew all control rods at once

details.summary: In 1979 a partial meltdown at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania became the worst nuclear accident in US history. A stuck valve and confusing control room indicators led operators to make decisions that worsened the situation, though containment prevented significant radiation release.
details.whyItMatters: Three Mile Island effectively halted new nuclear plant construction in the US for decades. It transformed nuclear safety culture by emphasizing human factors and control room design.
takeaways: A stuck valve caused coolant loss that operators misinterpreted
About half the reactor core melted before the situation stabilized
No significant radiation escaped, but public confidence was shattered

faq.question: Why did the operators make the wrong decisions during the crisis?
faq.answer: The control room displayed over 100 simultaneous alarms with no prioritization. A critical relief valve appeared closed on instruments when it was actually stuck open. Operators relied on misleading readings and were not trained for this specific failure mode.

faq.question: Was anyone harmed by radiation from Three Mile Island?
faq.answer: The maximum radiation dose to nearby residents was estimated at about one millirem, less than a chest X-ray. Multiple studies found no significant increase in cancer rates in the surrounding area, though the psychological stress and community disruption were significant.
